title: Playing all-day parades in New Orleans for 75 cents
summary: Parades for unions and clubs ran from nine to five for 75 cents; he began at 14 or 15, proud of his hat and blue shirt, and remembers sore feet.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: A parade lasted from nine in the morning until five in the evening?
What were the occasions for the parades?
union or anything like that just walking. Labor Day, you know, they'd have about five or six bands, a big parade.
What -- you marched all over New Orleans?

All over, just walked. We'd stop and get something to eat and drink, and after they're finished and get a little rest, then they'd keep going and keep going. My feet looked like balloons when I got home. They're just soaking in hot water, cold water, hot water, cold water. Oh, boy. 75 cents. That's the kind of things that people -- I mean, kids nowadays don't know what hardship is, believe me.
How old were you when you started playing in parades?

About 14, 15. I was young, didn't care. I was just glad to be out and showing myself to the little girls, you know. All proud, you know. I had me a little hat, too, you know. Wear that rascal on the side. Sharp. I had a blue shirt, you know. The blue looked like denim and white pants. Oh, that was something. That was good, real nice.
And the parade was fun, too?
